section.label: Experience
section.title: A history of making things work.

positions.title: Technical Director
description: By far my favorite professional experience. I was the Technical Director of a small animation company with wonderful people for a number of years.

My duties as a Technical Director were much more varied than they would have been at a larger company. I managed security and technical support, I oversaw employee onboarding and technical workflow for producers and artists.
My favorite duties involved a great deal of programming.

Balancing other tasks, I also implemented a number of iterations of the company website and a number of very quick one-off websites that were related to requests for proposals or deliverables to clients.

The largest ongoing project was being the lead designer of many versions of internal animation workflow pipeline related tools. These applications were large, complex and gave me the opportunity to become very well versed in many aspects of full stack web development.
highlights: Managed security, technical support, employee onboarding, and technical workflows for producers and artists.
Implemented multiple company websites and short-turnaround sites for proposals and client deliverables.
Led design of internal animation pipeline tools involving complex full-stack applications.

positions.title: Scribbles and Ink S2 - Developer
description: Lead developer for the second iteration of PBS’s “Scribbles and Ink” interactive drawing game for children.
In the second iteration, I was in charge of a small team (2) to expand on the prior successful property.
As a design goal, the game was to be created in a modular manner that would simplify the creation of additional material in the form of behavioral components and editor tools for artists.
This involved a complete rewrite of the original codebase and provided an excellent opportunity to gain experience communicating with artists.
Much of the documentation for the game engine is in another language, which presented the (honestly quite fun) challenge of coding in the dark.

I was also tasked with implementing and later interacting with Google Analytics for various statistics of interest to the client. Not particularly challenging, but it was something of a career milestone to see actual data on how well the game was doing.
highlights: Led development of the second interactive drawing game and a small team.
Rewrote the codebase with modular behavioral components and artist editor tools to support new content.
Implemented Google Analytics for client reporting.

positions.title: Scribbles and Ink S1 - Lead Developer
description: Developer for the first iteration of PBS’s “Scribbles and Ink” interactive drawing game for children:
S&I was an interesting project, a mobile experience where users draw while interacting with professionally animated characters.

As a design goal, the experience needed to be playable on a wide range of devices. There was a great deal of interesting memory management and dynamic asset loading problems due to conflicts with the serializable nature of the editor of the game engine the game was authored in that were fun to solve.
highlights: Developed an interactive drawing experience featuring professionally animated characters.
Solved memory management and dynamic asset loading challenges to support a wide range of devices.

positions.title: Software Developer
description: My first professional experience as a developer. There was a great deal of interacting programmatically with Adobe After Effects rendering.
This provided some interesting challenges due to the age of the javascript engine that powered the scripting of After Effects at the time.

It later led to the development of a library that allows developers to interact with the After Effects scripting engine from Node.js, which became my most popular GitHub repository and led to some contract work down the line.
highlights: Automated Adobe After Effects rendering using its scripting engine.
Work later led to a library connecting Node.js to the After Effects scripting environment.

paragraphs: In my early days, I gravitated toward development rather unconventionally through my experiences as an animator. Adding programmatic expressions to animatable properties became a solution to speed up the creation of many animation projects.
From there, I gravitated toward full stack web development and have been as software developer for 10 years.

In my experience, a finished product is an exercise in efficient time management. My mind gravitates to implementations that have maximum logical purity, or most optimally abstracted, but one never has an infinite amount of time to finish a product, especially in the case of working by yourself.
A lot of the wisdom I’ve gained as a developer is knowing what corners to cut to in order to optimize the balance between speed and technical debt.
about.approach: I care about thoughtful systems and the practical decisions that get them shipped. My work balances clear abstractions, delivery speed, and the technical debt a team can afford.
